labels.description: The sentence on regulatory scrutiny now says Schwab becomes subject to increasing scrutiny as it grows "and expand[s] client offerings" rather than only as it grows.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the scope of the regulatory scrutiny risk is widened to cover expansion of client offerings (tied to the new digital asset offering); the apparent deletion of the closing sanctions sentence and the inadvertent-noncompliance paragraph is an extraction artifact (text after the bold page header on page 17 was dropped), and the full 2025 filing retains that text word for word.

labels.description: The factor drops the specific references to the SEC's equity market structure proposals, the federal banking agencies' proposed regulatory capital and long-term debt rules, and the FDIC's proposed brokered deposits amendment, and adds digital assets to the areas of regulatory change plus a statement that the Company anticipates giving clients increased access to trade digital assets including select cryptocurrencies under still-pending laws that could block the launch or limit its profitability.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: three named regulatory proposals are dropped and a new product area (digital asset and cryptocurrency trading) with its pending regulation is referenced; criterion 1 also applies for the new exposure.

labels.description: Against the unchanged Category II thresholds of $700 billion in assets and $75 billion in cross-jurisdictional activity, CSC's year-end total assets rise from approximately $480 billion (December 31, 2024) to approximately $491 billion (December 31, 2025) and cross-jurisdictional activity from approximately $27 billion to approximately $31 billion.
labels.rationale: criterion 4: two dollar figures measuring proximity to the Category II thresholds change beyond the date roll-forward; the only other edit is a dropped comma.

labels.description: No substantive change: the prior excerpt shows only the first paragraph, while the current excerpt also shows the paragraphs on claims by clients of third-party advisors, intellectual property infringement claims, and settlement and judgment exposure.
labels.rationale: minor: the difference is an extraction artifact (in the 2024 filing the second and third paragraphs follow the bold page header on page 18, which the section parser treats as a category and drops), and the full risk factor text is word-for-word identical (297 words) in both filings.

labels.description: The strategic transactions factor now names the acquisition of Forge in two places, as a transaction that could materially affect financial position and as one whose anticipated benefits may not be realized in a timely manner or at all.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: a new specific transaction and counterparty (the Forge acquisition) is referenced where the prior text spoke only of hypothetical transactions.

labels.description: New risk factor on the planned 2026 launch of direct client access to digital assets including spot cryptocurrency trading, covering custody, trading, settlement and liquidity risk, fraud and illicit activity, uncertain client demand, an evolving regulatory landscape, and the irreversibility of transactions and loss or theft of private keys.
The only change is hyphenation of "venture-capital backed" to "venture-capital-backed".
labels.rationale: minor: punctuation only, with identical meaning.

labels.description: No substantive change: the current excerpt shows the final two list items and the paragraph on return of capital, possible incomplete share repurchase authorization and dilution, which the prior excerpt omits.
labels.rationale: minor: the difference is an extraction artifact (in the 2024 filing the list continues after the bold page header on page 19, which the section parser drops), and the full risk factor text is word-for-word identical (159 words) in both filings.
